history.period: founding date of the Durgapur centre not documented (verify)
history.summary: ISKCON (International Society for Krishna Consciousness, founded 1966 by A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada) temple in Durgapur's A-Zone, formally named the Sri Sri Radha Madanmohan Mandir, housing statues of Radha and Krishna. It operates as an extension centre of ISKCON Mayapur, with a weekly Sunday feast (4:00-7:00 PM: kirtan, dancing, lecture and prasadam) and a sattvik food corner on the premises. IDENTITY CONFIRMED: official website iskcondurgapur.org and multiple listings place it at B-II/29, Netaji Subhash Road, A Zone, Durgapur 713204. The founding year of the Durgapur centre was not documented in sources found (verify).

name: Durgapur ISKCON Temple
town_description: Durgapur is a major industrial city in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal. The A-Zone is a central residential area of Durgapur; the temple sits on Netaji Subhash Road near Dhobighat.

travel.railway: Durgapur station; local buses/taxis to A-Zone
travel.road: B-II/29, Netaji Subhash Road, Dhobighat, A Zone, Durgapur 713204

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sunday afternoons for the weekly feast
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM-9:00 PM (Mangala arati 4:00 AM; sandhya arati 6:00 PM; exact midday schedule varies between sources - verify). Dress modestly; photography restrictions reported inside the temple.
